newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Rwanda genocide tribunal to rule on six suspects.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda genocide tribunal to rule on six suspects.

text.p: A tribunal on Rwanda's 1994 genocide is to decide on Thursday whether to continue to detain six suspects handed over by Kenya, the tribunal said on Tuesday.

The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda said in a statement the six men would appear before its president, Judge Laity Kama of Senegal, in Arusha town on Thursday for a decision on whether they should be released or their detention extended.
The tribunal said the six were among eight suspects arrested by Kenyan police in July and immediately transferred to the tribunal's headquarters in the northern Tanzanian town of Arusha.
It said six of the eight were not indicted by the tribunal and were only suspected of having taken part in the 1994 genocide of an estimated 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates in Rwanda.
The six were therefore only initially detained for 30 days.

The tribunal said the six included former prime minister Jean Kambanda, former newspaper editor Hassan Ngeze and Belgian Georges Ruggiu, a former journalist at Rwanda's Radio Television des Milles Collines and the only non-Rwandan held in Arusha.

The other three were Sylvain Nsabimana, a former government official in the southern Rwandan city of Butare, Gratien Kabiligi, a former colonel in the army's general staff, and Aloys Ntabakuze, former commander of a commando battalion.
The International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda was set up in 1994 to bring to justice leaders of the genocide sparked by the assassination of military strongman Juvenal Habyarimana.
Twenty-three suspects have been indicted and the tribunal holds 27 in custody in Arusha. Three trials are now in progress.
